CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Magelang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Magelang.
4. Regional House of Representatives of Magelang Regency, hereinafter referred to as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
7. Violence is any unlawful act, with or without using means, in the form of physical or verbal acts that endanger life or the body and/or result in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of basic human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the fields of politics, economy, law, social, culture and other aspects of life.
11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt entrapment or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
13. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
14. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Discrimination, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.

17. Safe house (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
18. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the environment and workplace, and/or a substitute family that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Recovery of victims is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence against women and children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically, or socio-culturally.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of women and children victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
21. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

19. Recovery of victims is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence against women and children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically, or socio-culturally.

22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL
Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection for women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is the obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.
On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 concerning the existence of such regulation. The existence of these regulations is felt to be not yet capable of providing maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to those legislative problems/issues, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.
Based on this thinking, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination that is able to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.
This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Government Responsibility up to the Participation of Government, Society and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.
In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding arrangements sourced from the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are not binding are expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

I. GENERAL
Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection for women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is the obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.
On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 concerning the existence of such regulation. The existence of these regulations is felt to be not yet capable of providing maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to those legislative problems/issues, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.
Based on this thinking, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination that is able to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.
This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Government Responsibility up to the Participation of Government, Society and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.
In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding arrangements sourced from the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are not binding are expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Magelang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Magelang.
4. Regional House of Representatives of Magelang Regency, hereinafter referred to as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
7. Violence is any unlawful act, with or without using means, in the form of physical or verbal acts that endanger life or the body and/or result in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of basic human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the fields of politics, economy, law, social, culture and other aspects of life.
11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt entrapment or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
13. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
14. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Discrimination, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
15. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of criminal acts of trafficking in persons in Magelang Regency.
16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
17. Safe house (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
18. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the environment and workplace, and/or a substitute family that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Recovery of victims is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence against women and children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically, or socio-culturally.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of women and children victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
21. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL
Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection for women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is the obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.
On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 concerning the existence of such regulation. The existence of these regulations is felt to be not yet capable of providing maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to those legislative problems/issues, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.
Based on this thinking, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination that is able to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.
This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Government Responsibility up to the Participation of Government, Society and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.
In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding arrangements sourced from the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are not binding are expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

I. GENERAL
Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection for women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is the obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.
On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 concerning the existence of such regulation. The existence of these regulations is felt to be not yet capable of providing maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to those legislative problems/issues, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.
Based on this thinking, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination that is able to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.
This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Government Responsibility up to the Participation of Government, Society and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.
In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding arrangements sourced from the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are not binding are expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
7. Violence is any unlawful act, with or without using means, in the form of physical or verbal acts that endanger life or the body and/or result in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of basic human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the fields of politics, economy, law, social, culture and other aspects of life.
11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt entrapment or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
13. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.

Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Discrimination, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.

17. Safe house (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.

19. Recovery of victims is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence against women and children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically, or socio-culturally.

22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Magelang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Magelang.
4. Regional House of Representatives of Magelang Regency, hereinafter referred to as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
7. Violence is any unlawful act, with or without using means, in the form of physical or verbal acts that endanger life or the body and/or result in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of basic human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the fields of politics, economy, law, social, culture and other aspects of life.
11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt entrapment or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
13. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
14. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Discrimination, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
15. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of criminal acts of trafficking in persons in Magelang Regency.
16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
17. Safe house (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
18. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the environment and workplace, and/or a substitute family that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Recovery of victims is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence against women and children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically, or socio-culturally.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of women and children victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
21. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 15
In addition to establishing P2TP2A as referred to in Article 14, in order to support the implementation of protection for women and children from acts of violence and discrimination, the Regent shall establish:
a. a task force on the criminal offense of trafficking in persons; and
b. a regional action committee for the elimination of the worst forms of child labor.

CHAPTER VI
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 9
Obligations and responsibilities in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence and discrimination are the shared responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Village Government;
c. Community; and
d. Family.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 20
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance on the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence and discrimination.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes: a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. monitoring; and
d. evaluation.
(3) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) is conducted in order to realize the objectives of protection of women and children from acts of violence and discrimination in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by Regional Apparatus that administer governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 21
(1) The Local Government is obligated to conduct supervision over the implementation of the protection of women and children from acts of violence and discrimination.
(2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out with the principles of being professional, transparent, and accountable.

Article 2
Letter a The principle of respect for human rights serves as the foundation for the concept of protection of women and children victims from acts of violence and discrimination, and constitutes respect for human rights as well as the dignity and worth of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila).
Letter b The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
Letter c The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children victims of acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and among groups.
Letter d The principle of victim protection, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, communities and the Regional Government are to fulfill the rights of women and victims of acts of violence as regulated in laws and regulations.
Letter e The principle of Empowerment is that every effort to protect women and children victims of violence must be oriented towards efforts to strengthen victims both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.
Letter f The principle of integration means that the series of activities to provide protection to women and children victims of violence will be implemented jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unified implementation.

Letter f Sufficiently clear.

(2) Financing assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the region's financial capacity, and shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER X
FINANCING

c. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and/or
d. other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL
Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection for women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is the obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.
On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 concerning the existence of such regulation. The existence of these regulations is felt to be not yet capable of providing maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to those legislative problems/issues, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.
Based on this thinking, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination that is able to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.
This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Government Responsibility up to the Participation of Government, Society and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.
In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding arrangements sourced from the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are not binding are expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Magelang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Magelang.
4. Regional House of Representatives of Magelang Regency, hereinafter referred to as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
7. Violence is any unlawful act, with or without using means, in the form of physical or verbal acts that endanger life or the body and/or result in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of basic human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the fields of politics, economy, law, social, culture and other aspects of life.
11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt entrapment or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
13. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
14. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Discrimination, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
15. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of criminal acts of trafficking in persons in Magelang Regency.
16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions normally.
17. Safe house (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
18. Social reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the environment and workplace, and/or a substitute family that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
19. Recovery of victims is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence against women and children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically, or socio-culturally.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of women and children victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
21. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward to the third degree.
22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Based on this thinking, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination that is able to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

I. GENERAL
Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection for women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is the obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.
On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 concerning the existence of such regulation. The existence of these regulations is felt to be not yet capable of providing maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to those legislative problems/issues, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.
Based on this thinking, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination that is able to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.
This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Government Responsibility up to the Participation of Government, Society and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.
In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding arrangements sourced from the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are not binding are expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

CHAPTER I

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
7. Violence is any unlawful act, with or without using means, in the form of physical or verbal acts that endanger life or the body and/or result in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
8. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of basic human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the fields of politics, economy, law, social, culture and other aspects of life.
11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt entrapment or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
12. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
13. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.

Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Discrimination, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services and rehabilitation to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.

22. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

CHAPTER X
FINANCING
Article 23
Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence and discrimination is sourced from:
a. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
c. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and/or
d. other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL
Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
Protection for women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is the obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as regulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.
On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 concerning the existence of such regulation. The existence of these regulations is felt to be not yet capable of providing maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of the community. In addition to those legislative problems/issues, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.
Based on this thinking, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination that is able to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.
This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Government Responsibility up to the Participation of Government, Society and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.
In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding arrangements sourced from the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government and other Sources that are not binding are expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

Article 24

(2) Financing assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the region's financial capacity, and shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
